title: sre-weekly-update-2026-05-16
content:
SRE Weekly Update — 2026-05-16
Owner: Liam Chen (on behalf of eng-sre)
Collaborators: Priya Desai, Mateo Alvarez, Jordan Kim, Nadia Hassan

Summary
- Quiet week overall for platform availability: 99.94% cluster-wide uptime across hosted inference tier.
- One medium-severity incident (INC-2026-141) related to Autoscaler thrash affecting Dedicated pools; mitigated and postmortem in progress.
- SLO picture: query latency SLO (p95 < 120ms) degraded slightly due to bursty traffic on Tue — currently projected to meet monthly target but we’re watching tail latency.
- On-call: handoff completed without gaps; added an extra escalator for weekend coverage.

This week — highlights
1) Incident INC-2026-141 — Autoscaler thrash (Closed)
   - Timeline: 2026-05-12 22:10 UTC — 2026-05-13 03:40 UTC
   - Impact: Short-lived increases in enqueue latency for dedicated pools in us-west-2, CPU/GPUs cycled and nodes repeatedly added/removed causing request queueing.
   - Root cause (preliminary): A recent rollout of the new scaling policy (RED-2098) interacted poorly with sudden multi-tenant job spikes; the cool-down logic did not properly account for transient GPU startup tail.
   - Mitigation: Rolled back policy to previous stable version at 2026-05-12 23:05 UTC; applied temporary increased cool-down (20m) and additional logging.
   - Customer impact: ~3 customers saw increased per-request latency and 5% error bump on some routes; no data loss.
   - Next steps: full RCA due 2026-05-20 (owner: Priya Desai). Follow-up ticket: RED-2147. Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-141+postmortem

2) Latency SLOs and Observability
   - p50/p95/p99 for API generation (hosted-api) for the week: 18ms / 110ms / 420ms. p95 slipped close to SLO during autoscaler thrash window.
   - Embeddings service SLO (p99 < 2s) met comfortably this week; observed improved cache hit-rate after cache warm-up work.
   - Action: add a dashboard panel to show autoscaler activity correlated with tail latency — assigned to Mateo (RED-2152).

3) Maintenance & Deployments
   - Canaries: infra/canary-runner v1.14 deployed Wed (no regressions).
   - Scheduled maintenance: minor kernel patch on dedicated hosts in eu-central-1 planned for 2026-05-23 02:00-04:00 UTC — low impact window. Eng-ops to notify affected customers.

4) Capacity & Cost
   - Dedicated pool usage: 72% average across clusters; short bursts pushed node counts up in us-west-2 on Tue.
   - Capacity recommendation: provision a reserve burst pool for high-variance workloads (proposal in RED-2160).

On-call handoffs and rotations - Current on-call week: 2026-05-09 → 2026-05-16
   - Primary: Jordan Kim (handoff done 2026-05-16 09:00 UTC)
   - Secondary: Nadia Hassan
   - Escalation: Priya Desai (weekend extra coverage)
   - Notable handoff notes: temporary override applied for autoscaler alerts to reduce noise; new alert threshold for node-start-time (10m) added to prevent alert storming.

Open action items (owner, due)
- Priya: RCA for INC-2026-141 (draft by 2026-05-20) — includes mitigation timeline and deployment checklist.
- Mateo: Dashboard linking autoscaler events to p95 tail (RED-2152) — due 2026-05-19.
- Liam: Draft proposal for burst reserve pool (RED-2160) — due 2026-05-27.
- Jordan: Review and tighten alert runbooks for node flapping — due 2026-05-22.

Meeting notes / standups
- SRE weekly sync (2026-05-14)
   - Agenda: incident review, SLOs, upcoming maintenance, hiring update.
   - Decisions: accelerate autoscaler rollback test harness; add a simulated spike job to CI to test scaling heuristics.
- Postmortem working group met (2026-05-15) to draft incident narrative and identify testing gaps.

Customer & CS handoffs
- CS notified three impacted customers on 2026-05-13 with incident summary and mitigation steps. Follow-up outreach scheduled as part of postmortem.
- Support KB item to be created for "Transient latencies during autoscaler activity" — owner: Nadia — due 2026-05-21.

Risks & concerns
- Autoscaler tuning remains the top near-term risk for Dedicated pools — edge cases with startup latency and multi-tenant spikes.
- Capacity fragmentation: several customers have many small reserved nodes leading to allocation inefficiencies. Ops to propose consolidation plan.

Planned work next week
- Finalize INC-2026-141 postmortem and publish to Confluence.
- Implement observed-mode rollout for new scaling policy (simulate spikes before full rollout).
- Begin implementation of burst reserve pool design (RED-2160) — spike prototype due EOW.
- Triage long-tail alerts and reduce noisy alerts by 30% (Jordan).

Notes to self / informal
- Remember to escalate any performance anomalies to Priya immediately during high-traffic events.
- We should run the spike-sim job on staging nightly for a week before enabling autoscaler policy 2.0.

Relevant links and tickets
- INC-2026-141 (PagerDuty): PD-INC-2026-141
- RCA ticket: RED-2147
- Autoscaler policy rollout: RED-2098
- Burst pool proposal: RED-2160
- Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-141+postmortem

If anything missing or you want deeper metrics, ping me in #sre-ops or DM.

-- Liam
